approach: Add InterventionCategory::Mistake ("mistake"; ALL becomes 9 entries). One rule, records::is_mistake(category, what), decides what a mistake is: category mistake, or category other with `what` starting "Mistake:" (documented in a doc comment there; stored records are never rewritten). A new pure status::mistake_report(&Records) returns a MistakeReport: total, counts per class (class_of_work), counts per cause, and prevention proposals. The cause of a mistake is the cause text of its recorded introspection, grouped by introspect::normalise; a mistake with no recorded introspection counts under "no cause recorded". One proposal per normalised cause, carrying the prevention text and its kind shown as check (code-check), knowledge (default) or design change, plus the introspection ids and the number of mistakes it covers. StatusView gets a `mistakes` field apart from interventions_by_category. Athena::mistakes() exposes the report. display::mistakes renders it (status prints it when total > 0), and display::audit_report(report, Option<&Audited>) renders the audit output. Command::Audit in main.rs computes and prints the mistake report before calling athena.audit, so it prints when the audit is None (nested run) or when the audit errors; JSON output is one object with mistakes, audit (nullable) and invocation. Introspecting a mistake event adds a top-level `mistake_guidance` key to the introspection prompt asking for the check or knowledge that would have prevented it. README, CHANGELOG and the category table in docs/design/athena-v0.md name the category. Every criterion maps to a named test.

decisions.choice: Compute counts and proposals in code from stored records (pure mistake_report over Records); no new record type.
decisions.reason: No schema change or migration. Legacy 'Mistake:' records follow the same rule. The function is unit-testable and shared by status, status JSON and audit. The introspection record already holds cause, prevention_kind and prevention.

rejected.option: A new proposal record type for mistake prevention
rejected.why: Adds a schema and migration the request does not need.

rejected.option: Rewrite legacy 'other' records to category mistake
rejected.why: Out of scope; records are immutable.

decisions.choice: Cause = the introspection's cause text, grouped by normalise(); class = the intervention's class_of_work.
decisions.reason: A mistake has no cause field; the introspection is where the cause is recorded, and normalise already exists for comparing cause text. Mistakes with no introspection are still counted, under 'no cause recorded'.

rejected.why: That is a class of failure, not a cause. It could still be added later.

rejected.option: Add a cause field to Intervention
rejected.why: Schema change; deny_unknown_fields would make older readers reject new records.

decisions.choice: Print the mistake report in Command::Audit before calling athena.audit, and render through display::audit_report so tests can call it with Some and None.
decisions.reason: The brief requires the counts to print when no job audit is produced (audit returns Ok(None) for a nested run). Printing first also survives an audit error.

rejected.option: Print after the audit, as in the earlier attempt
rejected.why: It sat behind the early return, so no counts appeared when audit returned None.

decisions.choice: Status prints the mistakes line only when total > 0; audit always prints it ('mistakes none' when zero).
decisions.reason: Existing status tests and output stay unchanged when there are no mistakes. The audit states plainly that there were none.

rejected.option: Always print a mistakes line in status
rejected.why: Risks breaking existing output assertions for no gain.

decisions.choice: Do not touch reading.rs unless a compile or test need appears; it only constructs CorrectedOutput/AnsweredQuestion interventions.
decisions.reason: Smallest change; nothing there depends on the category set.

rejected.option: Edit reading.rs to be listed as a deliverable
rejected.why: It would be a change with no behavior behind it.

files.purpose: Add the Mistake variant (ALL becomes 9, as_str "mistake"), a documented `is_mistake(category, what)` rule and Intervention::is_mistake, plus unit tests.
Add MistakeReport, CauseCount and MistakeProposal types, the pure mistake_report(&Records), Athena::mistakes(), and the StatusView.mistakes field. Unit tests, including the legacy prefix.
Add the top-level `mistake_guidance` prompt key for mistake events (category mistake, or legacy other with the 'Mistake:' prefix).
No logic change expected, since the error text is built from ALL. Add the test for accepting mistake and rejecting an unknown category with an error listing it.
Add display::mistakes and display::audit_report. Status prints the mistakes lines when total > 0.
Command::Audit prints the mistake report before athena.audit and handles None and JSON. Update the --category help text to list mistake.
Audit output tests: counts with an audit, counts when audit returns None (nested).
Prompt-guidance test, same-cause aggregation test, and the binary `athena audit` test under ATHENA_NESTED.
Status text and JSON test for per-class and per-cause counts, the legacy record test, and the docs mention test.
Record the mistake category, the mistakes report in status and audit, and the prevention proposals.
Mention the mistake category beside athena intervene and the mistakes report in status and audit.
Add `mistake` to the category list in the intervention record table row (line ~366), and note the 'Mistake:' legacy rule.

steps: Read the existing status test in lifecycle.rs (line ~1118) and the Model in introspection.rs so the new tests reuse the fixtures.

records.rs: add the Mistake variant and extend ALL (length 9) and as_str. Add is_mistake(category, what) with a doc comment that states the text-prefix rule for legacy 'other' records, and Intervention::is_mistake. Add unit tests.

status.rs: add the report types and mistake_report(&Records). It loops over records.interventions with is_mistake, finds the recorded introspection by `intervention` id, and groups causes by normalise. It builds proposals from the introspection prevention_kind and prevention. Add Athena::mistakes() and StatusView.mistakes. Add unit tests.
introspect.rs: in user_prompt add `mistake_guidance` when the event is a mistake. Check that the legacy-prefix event also gets it.
display.rs: add mistakes() and audit_report(); call mistakes() from status() after the interventions line when total > 0.
main.rs: restructure Command::Audit to print the report first (text) or an object with mistakes/audit/invocation (JSON); update the --category help text.
manage.rs and the tests: add the criterion 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 tests under the names given in the demonstrations.
Update README.md, CHANGELOG.md and docs/design/athena-v0.md, and add the docs mention test.
Run cargo fmt --all, then cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings, then cargo test --locked, and write the criterion-to-test map in the final note.

risks.risk: Adding an enum variant breaks exhaustive matches or tests that assume 8 categories.
risks.mitigation: The only matches I found use a wildcard (introspect.rs line 1219). Run cargo test --locked and fix the rest at compile time.

risks.risk: Changing the JSON from `athena audit --json` could break a consumer.
risks.mitigation: Keep the `audit` and `invocation` keys and add `mistakes`; audit is null when none was produced. No existing test reads that output (grep in the tests found none).

risks.risk: A new status line shifts existing output assertions.
risks.mitigation: Print the mistakes lines only when total > 0; JSON adds a key without removing any.

risks.risk: The earlier attempt was rejected for a missing audit test and a print behind the early return.
risks.mitigation: Criterion 3 has named tests at the library and binary level that cover the Some, None and error cases. The producer lists each criterion against a test name before finishing.

demonstrations.method: Tests: records.rs unit tests `mistake_is_a_category_and_in_all` and `parse_accepts_mistake`; manage.rs test `intervene_accepts_mistake_and_rejects_unknown_category_listing_mistake` runs athena.intervene with category "mistake" (committed record has category Mistake) and with "bogus" (error text contains "mistake").
demonstrations.observes: InterventionCategory::ALL contains Mistake, parse("mistake") is Some, the bogus category errors and the message lists mistake.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the Mistake variant, parse returns None, intervene bails on "mistake", and the ALL assertion fails.

demonstrations.method: lifecycle.rs test `status_reports_mistakes_per_class_and_per_cause_apart_from_categories`: intervene with category mistake in classes docs and code (e.g. 3 mistakes: 2 docs, 1 code); a scripted introspection model gives two with the same cause text (differing only in case or punctuation) and one with a different cause. Asserts athena.status().mistakes (total 3, by_class docs 2 / code 1, by_cause two entries 2 and 1), asserts display::status text contains a 'mistakes 3' line with class and cause counts, and runs the binary `athena status --json` asserting json["mistakes"]["by_class"] and ["by_cause"] while interventions_by_category has only "mistake": 3.
demonstrations.observes: Mistake counts per class and per cause in the text and in the JSON, in fields separate from interventions_by_category.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the mistakes field there is no "mistakes" key in JSON and no mistakes line in status text, so the assertions fail.

demonstrations.method: auditor.rs tests `the_audit_output_reports_mistakes_per_class_and_per_cause` (landed job, mistakes logged via athena.intervene, athena.audit returns Some, assert display::audit_report(&athena.mistakes()?, Some(&audited)) contains the total, each class count, each cause count and still the finding) and `the_audit_output_reports_mistakes_when_no_audit_is_produced` (nested athena: audit returns None, display::audit_report(.., None) contains the same counts). introspection.rs test `athena_audit_prints_mistakes_before_any_audit` runs the real binary `athena audit latest` with ATHENA_NESTED set (and a variant on a job-less repository where the audit errors) and asserts stdout contains the mistake counts per class and cause.
demonstrations.observes: The audit command's output lists mistakes per class and per cause with a job audit, with None, and when the audit fails.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without printing before the early return, the None case and the binary case produce no mistake lines and the assertions fail.

demonstrations.method: introspection.rs tests `a_mistake_intervention_is_introspected_with_guidance_for_the_preventing_check_or_knowledge` (scripted model captures the prompt: category is "mistake" and `mistake_guidance` names the check or knowledge; non-mistake prompts lack the key) and `mistakes_with_the_same_cause_aggregate_into_one_proposal` (two mistake interventions whose recorded causes normalise equal, one other cause; mistake_report.proposals has 2 entries, the shared one with mistakes 2, two introspection ids, and a kind check/knowledge and prevention text from the record). A unit test in status.rs covers the kind mapping code-check->check, default->knowledge, design-change->design change.
demonstrations.observes: The introspection prompt asks for the preventing check or knowledge; the proposal names it; same-cause mistakes give one proposal.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the guidance key the prompt assertion fails; without grouping by normalised cause the proposal count is 3, not 2.

demonstrations.method: status.rs unit test `a_legacy_other_record_starting_mistake_colon_is_counted_and_not_rewritten` and records.rs test `is_mistake_rule`: an `other` intervention with what "Mistake: ..." counts, an `other` with "A mistake: ..." or "mistake in" does not, a category-mistake record counts once. The lifecycle test also checks the stored record file is byte-identical and interventions_by_category still shows "other". The rule is documented in the doc comment on is_mistake (a reviewer reads it).
demonstrations.observes: Legacy records are counted in status and the audit output, and the record on disk is unchanged.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the prefix rule the legacy record is absent from the totals and the assertions fail.

demonstrations.method: Run cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo test after the change.
demonstrations.observes: fmt and clippy print no diagnostics and every test passes, including the existing ones that match on InterventionCategory.

demonstrations.method: The status and audit tests above assert that the rendered text shows the mistake total, the recurring classes and causes (with counts above 1), and a 'prevention' line per proposal giving kind and text. README.md, CHANGELOG.md and the category row in docs/design/athena-v0.md are edited; a test in lifecycle.rs reads those three files with include_str! (or from the repo root) and asserts each contains "mistake". A fresh reader rating is prose-only and is done by the reviewer on the live output.
demonstrations.observes: The output shows how many mistakes, which classes and causes recur, and which prevention was proposed. The three docs mention the category.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the docs edits the include_str! assertions fail; without the proposal lines the output assertions fail.

open_questions: Mistake causes are free text from the model, so two mistakes only share a cause if their normalised text is equal. Whether to group by failure_class instead is a product choice the code cannot settle.

Whether `athena audit` under ATHENA_NESTED works in the test environment (nested::prepare builds a scratch copy) was not run. If it cannot, the binary test uses a job-less repository where the audit errors after the mistakes are printed.
reading.rs is a listed deliverable, but I found nothing in it that depends on the category set. I plan no edit unless the compiler requires one.
Whether the test Model captures the `mistake_guidance` key in the prompt depends on the scripted model passing the parsed prompt JSON; I read that it does (prompts: Vec<Value>).
